subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw default web_fetch SSRF handling allow mixed DNS result sets by dropping blocked addresses and pinning only allowed candidates, or should any blocked resolved address continue to fail the request?
rationale: The source fix is small, but it changes a default outbound security boundary and needs maintainer/security intent rather than automated policy guessing.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow web_fetch to proceed only when at least one resolved address is allowed, and pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat the current behavior as intentional strict SSRF policy and document trusted proxy or fake-IP configuration as the supported path for polluted DNS environments.

options.title: Make mixed-answer behavior opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an explicit operator-controlled policy for DNS-polluted environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow web_fetch to proceed only when at least one resolved address is allowed, and pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher.

likelyOwner.reason: The central SSRF boundary history points to steipete as the best available owner for deciding whether to relax this default.
